key_insight: APS-produced Fe79Zr6Si14Cu1 coatings remained predominantly crystalline, while increasing spray distance improved hardness and wear resistance at the expense of corrosion resistance.
engineering_relevance: A 90 mm spray distance offered the most favourable tested balance of hardness, wear resistance, and electrochemical behaviour.
method: Deposit low-glass-forming-ability Fe79Zr6Si14Cu1 coatings by atmospheric plasma spraying at varying spray distances.
Characterize phase composition, lamellar microstructure, and porosity.
Evaluate hardness, wear resistance, and electrochemical behaviour.
evidence_signal: XRD detected α-Fe(Si) and Fe–Zr intermetallic phases with no detectable amorphous fraction; coating porosity ranged from 2.2% to 4.9%.
watch_item: Longer spray distances increased porosity and interlamellar defects, so gains in hardness and wear resistance should not be assumed to improve corrosion performance.
paper_title: Phase Evolution and Structure–Property Relationships of Fe79Zr6Si14Cu1 Coatings with Low GFA Produced by Atmospheric Plasma Spraying
